title: Streamline artifact intake and shard contract simplification
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: The model artifact ingestion path currently supports multiple legacy manifest shapes and ad-hoc shard naming conventions. This increases memory usage at runtime, forces per-model special casing in the loader, and inflates cold-start latency when the shard negotiator enumerates assets.

Goal: Reduce format ambiguity and simplify the shard negotiation surface so the loader can deterministically pick a minimal activation plan. Deliverables: (1) a consolidated manifest schema that unifies 'weights', 'shards', and 'index' sections; (2) a lightweight manifest validator used by both ingest and runtime; (3) a deterministic shard activation algorithm with backoff-friendly retry semantics; (4) a thin adapter layer to gracefully accept legacy manifests during a one-quarter migration window.

Approach:
- Introduce an 'artifact intake' stage that runs as part of model publishing and emits a normalized manifest (manifest-v2) stored alongside model assets. The stage will run as a CI job for self-hosted ingestion and as a server-side task for hosted models.
- Implement a delta-based validator that checks required fields (architecture, dtype, shard_map, byte_offsets, tokenizer_signature) and emits corrective hints instead of hard failures for common legacy patterns.
- Replace the current negotiator with a two-pass planner: quick-pass (metadata-only, picks primary shards to satisfy min_mem) and activation-pass (streams exact byte ranges into memory with an async prefetch window). This reduces the number of synchronous model read operations during warmup.
- Provide a compatibility shim in the loader that can translate legacy sharding maps into the normalized shard_map; log a migration warning with a link to the PR and Confluence migration guide.

Metrics and success criteria: cold-start p50 token-init latency reduced by >=25% for large 13B+ models; peak memory overhead during boot reduced by >=15%; ingestion validation errors reduced by >90% after migration; fewer model-specific special-case branches in loader code (target: reduce special-case count from N to <=3).

Rollout plan: feature-flag the runtime changes behind 'manifest-v2' gate; deploy ingest normalization in staging for two weeks and validate by importing a representative bucket of customer models; enable gradual rollout to production with a 10/30/60 percent traffic ramp and telemetry checks (error rates, cold-start latency, memory footprint).

Backward compatibility: legacy manifests continue to be accepted via the shim for a 90-day opt-in migration period. After migration, we will emit deprecation warnings and provide tooling to rewrite manifests in-place.

Risks: malformed legacy manifests with missing byte ranges may require full re-ingest and could block automated migration. Mitigations include a 'repair mode' in the intake job that attempts to reconstruct byte ranges from index files where available, and a safety knob to force full reingestion for flagged models.
acceptance_criteria: manifest-v2 schema published and documented in Confluence with examples
ingest job emits normalized manifest for all test models in staging
loader reads normalized manifest without per-model special-case branching in the hot path
cold-start p50 measured improvement >=25% on representative 13B/70B workload
compat shim logs migration warnings and provides rewrite tool for legacy manifests
comments: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — validated that most internal models have predictable shard layouts; prototype manifest-v2 accepted by infra. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INGEST/manifest-v2-spike
2026-02-28: Design review with runtime and infra — agreed on two-pass planner and async prefetch window. Action: Miguel to draft API for manifest validator.
2026-03-05: Initial PR opened for manifest validator and normalization job. GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3256 — needs unit tests for edge cases (non-contiguous shards)
2026-03-09: Load-testing in staging showed 18% cold-start p50 improvement on 13B models with prototype planner; need further optimization on prefetch concurrency to hit target.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed shim approach — no secrets handled, but recommended audit logs for manifest rewrites. Added to next iteration.
implementation_notes: Schema fields: version, model_id, architecture, shard_map (list of objects with shard_id, href, checksum, byte_range), tokenizer_signature, dtype_map
Validator will be implemented in Go (ingest) and Rust (runtime) to reuse existing assets; keep validator behavior identical across languages
Prefetch window tunable exposed in runtime config (prefetch_bytes, max_parallel_fetches)
Add telemetry: manifest_version, normalized_manifest_emitted (bool), legacy_shim_used (bool), plan_pass_durations_ms
